title: The Sovereignty Problem: Which Dual-Use Governance Frameworks Require Ceding Data Sovereignty?

original_idea.body:
# The Sovereignty Problem: Which Dual-Use Governance Frameworks Require Ceding Data Sovereignty?

**Problem:** For Global South countries to use tiered access programs, they may need to submit to US/EU identity verification infrastructure, potentially ceding digital sovereignty.

**Direction:** Analyze 4 tiered access frameworks (OpenAI Trusted Access, Anthropic RSP, EU GPAI Code, NIST AI 800-1) for sovereignty implications of their identity and monitoring provisions. Map which data flows to US/EU infrastructure are required. Assess whether BRICS countries could implement equivalent governance without such flows.

**Why it matters:** Governance frameworks that require sovereignty concessions will be rejected by many states, creating the regulatory arbitrage problem. Understanding sovereignty implications is essential for multilateral governance design.

**Relevant context:** BRICS AI governance declaration 2025; India AI Impact Summit 2026; Global South equity; OpenAI Trusted Access KYC.
